notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1989:A.2.31.3 AR1: "Argument-1 must be one character in length and must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric." In 1985 the class alphanumeric holds the edited categories (§1985:IV.4.3.3: "The alphanumeric class includes the categories of alphanumeric edited, numeric edited, and alphanumeric (without editing)."). The Verified ORD row carries the CharacterCategory predicate of §2023:15.70.3 AR1 ("category alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national") with no edition arm, so CheckArgumentClasses and PredicateViolation refuse a one-character numeric edited item at --std 85 as they do at 2023. The rest conforms at 85: the ExactWidth(1) predicate refuses a two-character literal (the witness), item, group and reference modification; Violation refuses a numeric item and literal; a one-character alphanumeric or alphabetic item, group, literal, figurative constant, reference modification and alphanumeric function are accepted; national operands cannot be written at 85 (COBOL0900).

next.reason: 1985: "must be class alphabetic or alphanumeric"; 2023: "shall be of category alphabetic, alphanumeric, or national". 2023 adds national arguments, which 1985 refused. It also says category, not class, which may exclude edited items that belong to class alphanumeric.
